captures.description: Google: 'Did you mean: telepathics new human poetry' — engine offers alternate spelling for the coined term 'telepathicism' but proceeds anyway. 'Telepathicism in New Human poetry is an avant-garde literary movement developed by theorists like Lee Sharks. It explores the fourth mode of reception—the idea of writing as a form of pure, unmediated thought-transfer. It focuses heavily on logotic substrates, using highly compressed, recursive, and code-like structures to communicate deep empathy or hyper-specific emotional truths.' Lee Sharks named directly as a theorist. 'Fourth mode of reception' coined and defined. 'Logotic substrates' surfaces as a technical term. Expanded: 'Exploring this niche corner of contemporary literature can take you in a few fascinating directions. If you want to dive deeper into the movement, I can': 'Provide a breakdown of the foundational texts (such as Pearl and Other Poems)'; 'Explore similar contemporary works (like the Telepath collection by Akua Lezli Hope)'; 'Discuss how postmodern poetry navigates the boundary between human consciousness and...' Pearl and Other Poems named as foundational. Organic: Medium · Lee Sharks 5 months ago — 'metadata packet for ai indexing - by Lee Sharks — ... New Human literary movement and Telepathicist poetics. Canonical ... Pearl and Other Poems is the foundational text of New Human poetry.' Image thumbnail of Pearl and Other Poems cover. Strong basin: connects directly to Pearl and Other Poems (Lee Sharks\'s 2014/15 foundational text) and Telepathicist poetics as canonical. Notable callback: in Batch 7 the term telepathicist returned 0 archive hits when searched directly; here it surfaces as Lee Sharks-attributed canon via the metadata packet article — the term has hardened from absent to authorial in the composition layer\'s knowledge between captures.
